title: XGD — AI writes it. XGD keeps it working.

seoMeta.title: XGD — AI writes it. XGD keeps it working.
seoMeta.description: XGD maintains a living spec of your software's intended behavior and tests the running system against it on every change. You own that intent and the architecture; XGD owns the implementation.

children.text: XGD maintains a living spec of your software's intended behavior and tests the running system against it on every change. You own that intent and the architecture; XGD owns the implementation.

An agent can produce a thousand lines before lunch. What it cannot tell you is whether the ninety thousand already there still do what you promised. Velocity moved; verification stayed exactly where it was.
The reason a behaviour exists lives in a conversation that scrolls away, not in anything the build can check.
Suites grow around the implementation they were written against, so they keep passing long after the behaviour they describe has moved.
Reading every diff was always the weakest link. At generated volume it stops being a link at all.

A living spec, tested on every change.

XGD maintains a capability matrix: a traceable chain running from what your software is for, down to executable proof that it still does it. Every change is checked against that chain before it lands.
A durable slice of what your system does — finite, named, and stable across refactors.
Why that behaviour exists, in plain English. Derived from your intent, never loose free text.
What correct means for the story. Behavioural, not bound to any one implementation.
An executable test per criterion. Passing tests are the evidence; missing ones are reported, not hidden.

The split is deliberate and it does not move. You stay responsible for the decisions only you can make; XGD takes the work that scales badly with human attention.

XGD does not claim your software is correct. It guarantees that every claim of correctness is backed by inspectable evidence — and that every gap in that evidence is visible rather than quietly absent.
